message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on the auction for the yellow property group.

I have $889 and a dark blue monopoly. The yellow auction is at $74, so I need to decide if $75 is worth the risk of missing a big property hit.

p2 is maxed out at $74 and cannot raise further. p4 has only $29, so they will drop out. p1 could bid higher if I take the lead. I still lack Ventnor to complete the yellow set.

p4 owns many properties but only $29 cash. If they go bankrupt, Ventnor could come up for auction later. I am also calculating the rent threat from p1's orange hotels.

New York Avenue with three houses costs $650. After a $75 bid I would have $814 left, so I could survive that hit. Virginia Avenue with three houses costs $500.

p2 has three houses on Virginia, three on States, and two on St Charles. That is a legal even build. The rent from those three properties totals $1,000.

I am weighing whether to bid $75 and claim the yellow property. p2 is already maxed out, so I would eliminate them from the auction. Only p1 could then bid against me with $320. I am also considering that p2 does not actually own any yellows, so blocking them from acquiring one may be strategically useful.

Neither p2 nor p1 owns any yellows, so no one completes a set by winning this auction. If I acquire Marvin Gardens, I would hold two of the three yellows alongside my existing Atlantic Avenue. p4 would also hold two yellows if they win, needing only Ventnor to complete the set.

I am now weighing whether to let p2 win at $74 and force them to zero cash, or to bid $75 and take the property myself. If p2 wins, they would be extremely vulnerable to rent. If I win, I would spend $75 and gain a landing spot or future trade piece.

I am now favoring the $75 bid. I would keep two of the three yellows and block p4 from ever completing that set without trading with me. p2 winning at $74 would leave them with only a random property and no strategic threat.

A completed yellow set would be extremely strong, but building it requires a large cash outlay. I should prioritize my dark blue houses first, since they cost $200 each and are more urgent.

I calculated that building two houses on each dark blue would leave only $89, which is too thin to survive a $650 New York rent or a $500 Virginia rent. I could instead build one house on Boardwalk alone for $200 and keep $689, or one on each for $400 and keep $489. My prior strategy says to wait until the cash cushion is safe before building. A $75 bid is cheap enough to fit within this approach.

I am now considering a higher bid of $100 or $120 to discourage p1. p1 has only $320 cash and is in jail, so they may not want to spend heavily on a non-monopoly property.

I will bid $75 and stay quiet about my ceiling. p2 cannot raise further, so I am confident of winning. I will not overpay by bidding higher immediately. I am drafting a short public message to announce my bid.
